This time, I want specific individual boroughs (not an overall city-wide pattern) that fall into one of these two categories:
- HOT SPOT: a borough with a high Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents that is ALSO surrounded by other high-Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents neighboring boroughs
- COLD SPOT: a borough with a low Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents that is ALSO surrounded by other low-Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents neighboring boroughs

Look at each borough together with its neighbors from the adjacency list, and identify any that qualify. Explain your reasoning, including a computed value for each borough you name. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. For implementation including statistical method such as Moran's I, directly use only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

End your response with exactly one line listing every borough you identified, using HH for hot spot and LL for cold spot, and including a computed value for each:

Thought: Load dataset and adjacency, compute global mean, deviations, neighbor deviation sums, and raw local I_i for each borough; print these to choose candidates. 
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_crime_first_half_2014.csv')
adj = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv')

# Compute global mean
x_mean = df['value'].mean()
print("Global mean:", x_mean)

# Build adjacency dict
adj_dict = {}
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, []).append(n)

# Map values by borough
val_dict = dict(zip(df['borough'], df['value']))

# Compute local I_i = (x_i - mean) * sum_j (x_j - mean)
results = []
for b in df['borough']:
    xi = val_dict[b]
    x_dev = xi - x_mean
    neighbors = adj_dict.get(b, [])
    # Only consider neighbors present in val_dict
    neighbors = [n for n in neighbors if n in val_dict]
    neigh_dev_sum = sum(val_dict[n] - x_mean for n in neighbors)
    Ii = x_dev * neigh_dev_sum
    results.append((b, xi, len(neighbors), neigh_dev_sum, Ii))

res_df = pd.DataFrame(results, columns=['borough','x_i','num_neighbors','neighbor_dev_sum','I_i'])
print(res_df.sort_values('I_i', ascending=False))
```

Thought: Symmetrize adjacency so every borough has full neighbor list, then recompute local I_i for each borough.
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_crime_first_half_2014.csv')
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Global mean
x_mean = df['value'].mean()
print("Global mean:", x_mean)

# Symmetrize adjacency
adj_dict = {}
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    # only include if neighbor is in boroughs
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, set()).add(n)
    adj_dict.setdefault(n, set()).add(b)

# Ensure keys for all boroughs
for b in df['borough']:
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, set())

# Map values
val = dict(zip(df['borough'], df['value']))

# Compute local I_i
results = []
for b in df['borough']:
    xi = val[b]
    x_dev = xi - x_mean
    neighbors = [n for n in adj_dict[b] if n in val]
    neigh_dev_sum = sum(val[n] - x_mean for n in neighbors)
    Ii = x_dev * neigh_dev_sum
    results.append((b, xi, neighbors, neigh_dev_sum, Ii))
res = pd.DataFrame(results, columns=['borough','x_i','neighbors','neighbor_dev_sum','I_i'])
print(res[['borough','x_i','neighbors','neighbor_dev_sum','I_i']].sort_values('I_i', ascending=False))
```

Thought: Filter boroughs with x_i > mean and neighbor_dev_sum > 0 for hotspots, and x_i < mean and neighbor_dev_sum < 0 for coldspots, excluding 'City of London'. 
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load and prepare data
df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_crime_first_half_2014.csv')
adj = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv')
x_mean = df['value'].mean()
val = dict(zip(df['borough'], df['value']))

# Build symmetrized adjacency
adj_dict = {}
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, set()).add(n)
    adj_dict.setdefault(n, set()).add(b)
for b in df['borough']:
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, set())

# Collect local measures
records = []
for b in df['borough']:
    xi = val[b]
    if pd.isna(xi):
        continue
    x_dev = xi - x_mean
    neighbors = [n for n in adj_dict[b] if n in val and not pd.isna(val[n])]
    neigh_dev_sum = sum(val[n] - x_mean for n in neighbors)
    records.append({'borough':b,'x_i':xi,'x_dev':x_dev,'neigh_dev_sum':neigh_dev_sum})

loc = pd.DataFrame(records)

# Hotspots: x_dev>0 and neigh_dev_sum>0
hot = loc[(loc['x_dev']>0)&(loc['neigh_dev_sum']>0)].sort_values(['x_dev','neigh_dev_sum'],ascending=False)
# Coldspots: x_dev<0 and neigh_dev_sum<0
cold = loc[(loc['x_dev']<0)&(loc['neigh_dev_sum']<0)].sort_values(['x_dev','neigh_dev_sum'])

print("Potential hotspots:")
print(hot[['borough','x_i','neigh_dev_sum']])
print("\nPotential coldspots:")
print(cold[['borough','x_i','neigh_dev_sum']])
```

Thought: Filter boroughs where borough value > mean AND all neighbors > mean for hotspots; and borough value < mean AND all neighbors < mean for coldspots.
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data and adjacency
df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_crime_first_half_2014.csv')
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Compute mean
mean_val = df['value'].mean()

# Value dict
val = dict(zip(df['borough'], df['value']))

# Symmetric adjacency
adj_dict = {}
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, set()).add(n)
    adj_dict.setdefault(n, set()).add(b)
for b in df['borough']:
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, set())

# Identify hotspots and coldspots
hot = []
cold = []
for b, xi in val.items():
    if pd.isna(xi):
        continue
    neighbors = [n for n in adj_dict[b] if n in val and not pd.isna(val[n])]
    if not neighbors:
        continue
    # Check all
    if xi > mean_val and all(val[n] > mean_val for n in neighbors):
        hot.append((b, xi))
    if xi < mean_val and all(val[n] < mean_val for n in neighbors):
        cold.append((b, xi))

print("Hotspots all neighbors above mean:", hot)
print("Coldspots all neighbors below mean:", cold)
```
